Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

what’s the matter? phrase

also what’s wrong?, what’s wrong with you?

classical

Traupman 92
Traupman 409: what’s wrong with you?, quid est tibi? or quid est tēcum?
Plaut. Curc. 236: sed quid tibi est?

Quid tibi est?

Examples

  • «Quid tibi est? Aurēs dolent?»

    “What’s the matter? Do your ears hurt?”Libellus I, Iter in Lūsitāniam

  • quid agis? — Vīvō. — Nempe ut dignus es. sed quid tibi est?

    How are you? — Alive. — As you deserve, no doubt. But what’s wrong with you?Plaut. Curc. 235–236

See also why so sad?, what happened?.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: pp. 92, 409, checked against the searchable text of the book on 29 October 2026 and 9 November 2026.
